tagline: An eastern town of fruit and gemstones, with an old riverside community, mountains, and the sea
introHtml:
Chanthaburi is an eastern town that packs a lot into one province. In town you'll find the Chanthaboon Riverside Community, a long row of old wooden houses along the river, the big Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception, and a gem market where people have bought and sold stones for generations.

Outside town there's Phlio Waterfall, Khao Khitchakut where people climb to pay respects at the Buddha's footprint during the cool season, and beaches around Laem Sing and Chao Lao for a swim. When fruit season hits, roughly April to June, durian, rambutan, and mangosteen all ripen at once, and that's when the most people make the trip to Chanthaburi.
bestTime: Fruit season, April–June, for fresh orchard durian, rambutan, and mangosteen. November–February is cool and good for climbing Khao Khitchakut and heading to the beach.

highlights.name: Chanthaboon Riverside Community
highlights.blurb: A long stretch of old wooden houses along the Chanthaburi River, with coffee shops, dessert stalls, and local snacks to keep you walking all day. This is the town's signature image.

highlights.name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
highlights.blurb: A large Gothic-style church on the river, across from the riverside community. Inside is a statue of the Virgin Mary adorned with gemstones set by Chanthaburi craftsmen.

highlights.name: Chanthaburi Gem Market
highlights.blurb: A gem-trading district in the heart of town, busiest on weekends. People sit cutting and trading stones right along the street, a sight that's hard to find anywhere else.

highlights.name: Khao Khitchakut
highlights.blurb: A tall mountain people climb to pay respects at the Buddha's footprint and the sacred boulder. It opens only during the cool season, roughly January to March.

highlights.name: Phlio Waterfall
highlights.blurb: A forest waterfall with schools of soro brook carp in its clear pools. It's a short walk in, shady and good for a swim, and one of the province's best-known falls.

highlights.name: Chanthaburi Fruit Season
highlights.blurb: From April to June, durian, rambutan, mangosteen, and longkong all ripen together. You can visit orchards to eat straight off the tree, plus fruit markets all over town.

foodScene.name: Sen Chan Noodles
foodScene.note: Sen chan rice noodles are the province's signature, made into crab pad thai with sen chan and tom yum noodles. You'll find them all over town and can buy dried noodles to take home.

foodScene.name: Seafood
foodScene.note: Chanthaburi meets the sea around Laem Sing, Chao Lao, and Pak Nam Khaem Nu, with seafood spots serving crab, prawns, oysters, and fresh fish by the water.

foodScene.name: Durian and Orchard Fruit
foodScene.note: In fruit season there's Mon Thong and Phuang Manee durian, rambutan, and mangosteen sold at markets and orchards, plus fried durian and other processed snacks.

foodScene.name: Sweets and Riverside Treats
foodScene.note: The Chanthaboon Riverside Community has khanom khuai ling, egg sponge cakes, topped crispy rice crackers, and sen chan noodles to snack on at the old shops.

foodScene.name: Mu Liang and Local Dishes
foodScene.note: Chanthaburi has mu liang, rakam nam phrik, and dishes made with sour rakam fruit that are local specialties hard to find elsewhere.

foodScene.name: Mu Liang Noodles and Street Food in Town
foodScene.note: In the town center there are noodles, rice with curry, and street snacks at the markets to try as you wander around.

foodScene.name: Cafes in the Old Town
foodScene.note: The riverside community and the area around town have cafes set in old wooden houses and coffee shops with river views to take a break in.

foodScene.name: Pepper and Processed Products
foodScene.note: Chanthaburi has grown pepper for a long time, with fresh pepper, green peppercorns, and processed products sold as souvenirs all over town.

attractions.name: Chanthaboon Riverside Community
attractions.blurb: A district of old wooden houses along the Chanthaburi River. Stroll past the old architecture and stop at coffee shops and local food stalls all day.

attractions.name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
attractions.blurb: A large Gothic-style church on the river, with a gem-adorned statue of the Virgin Mary and stained glass to see inside.

attractions.name: Chanthaburi Gem Market
attractions.blurb: A gem-trading district in the heart of town that buzzes on weekends. Watch the stone cutting and trading happen right on the street.

attractions.name: Khao Khitchakut
attractions.blurb: A tall mountain to climb and pay respects at the Buddha's footprint and the sacred boulder. It opens only during the cool season, roughly January to March.

attractions.name: Phlio Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A waterfall inside the national park with schools of soro brook carp in clear pools. It's a short walk in, shady, and good for a swim.

attractions.name: Chao Lao Beach–Laem Sing
attractions.blurb: The province's eastern coast, with sandy beaches and seafood spots by the water to sit and eat and take a swim.

attractions.name: Khuk Khi Kai and the Red Building, Laem Sing
attractions.blurb: Old buildings from the French occupation at the Laem Sing river mouth, telling the seaside history of Chanthaburi.

attractions.name: King Taksin's Shipyard
attractions.blurb: A historic site believed to be where ships were built in the time of King Taksin, now a place to learn about Chanthaburi's past.

itineraryIdeas: Chanthaburi 2D1N — riverside community and gem market
Chanthaburi for cafes and the old town
Chanthaburi for nature — Phlio Waterfall and Khao Khitchakut
Chanthaburi in fruit season — eating durian straight from the orchard
Chanthaburi by the sea — Chao Lao and Laem Sing
